answer: Coordinated-entry pricing works like a gale in reverse: each new identity must submit a unique cipher proving a distinct hardware enclave, costing real compute time per node. The rule enforces that any cluster of identities sharing a reef of network topology pays an escalating coordination fee proportional to cluster tightness, verified through latency fingerprints. Attacker cost scales superlinearly because forged enclaves still burn the fee per cluster, and tight coordination raises it further.
